hypothesis: If fleas, flies and blister beetles arise from putrefying matter rather than from parents, and produce only a larva that is not their own kind, their life-cycle accounts will not describe eggs laid by adults that develop into adults of the same kind.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. A kind supports the claim when its account states spontaneous generation from putrefying matter and does not state that females lay eggs which become adults of that kind. The claim is supported only if at least two of the three kinds (flea, fly, cantharides) are coded that way and none is coded as parental. Confidence 0.70.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. A kind refutes the claim when the account says eggs are laid and either names complete or holometabolous metamorphosis or names egg, larva, pupa and adult, and it does not affirm spontaneous generation. One such kind refutes the universal that these insects do not come from parents. Confidence is 0.80 if both flea and fly are parental, and 0.65 if only one kind is parental. If some coded kinds are parental and some are spontaneous, the verdict is mixed (confidence 0.55). If no kind has a usable account, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable (confidence 0.40).

test_contract.expected_observation: Accounts of fleas, flies and blister beetles say they arise from putrefying matter and do not describe a parental egg-to-adult cycle.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: An account of any one of those kinds describes eggs laid by the insect and development into an adult of the same kind.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A public species account that states the life cycle of a flea (Ctenocephalides felis), a fly (Musca domestica), and a blister beetle, the modern referent of cantharides. The first account in the candidate list that contains a reproduction or development section is used. Classification stubs are not accounts.
test_contract.inference_method: Code egg-laying, a four-stage or holometabolous life cycle, and spontaneous-generation wording with the phrases in rules. One parental life cycle refutes the claim that these insects do not come from parents.

interpretation: Cantharides is read as a blister beetle (Meloidae), with Lytta vesicatoria first and the other named accounts only if that page is not a life-cycle account. 'Produce only a scolex, not a creature of their own kind' is refuted by a stated development from egg to adult of the same species. The test uses published life-cycle prose, not a new rearing experiment.
caveats: Modern life-cycle accounts are expected, before reading them, to describe parental eggs. The phrases were fixed before download. A page that does not use those phrases is unstated, not a guess from memory.
Animal Diversity Web is a compilation. A code records what the account says.
